title: Simultaneous strict coefficient comparisons on ring-sheaf towers
statement:
Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ be a geometric morphism on small sites, with left-exact inverse image $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$. For $W=X,Y$ and $a=0,1,2$, let $R^a_{W,\bullet}$ be inverse sequences of commutative ring sheaves, with maps $i^{ab}_W:R^a_{W,\bullet}\to R^b_{W,\bullet}$ for $a\le b$, $i^{aa}=1$, $i^{02}=i^{12}i^{01}$. Let $\phi^a:u^{-1}R^a_{Y,\bullet}\to R^a_{X,\bullet}$ commute with all coefficient and sequence maps. A strict cochain system consists of possibly unbounded complexes of module sheaves with semilinear chain transitions; its morphisms commute with every transition [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Use the actual sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Put $F_aK=R^a_{X,\bullet}\otimes_{u^{-1}R^a_{Y,\bullet}}u^{-1}K$ and $S^{ab}_WK=R^b_{W,\bullet}\otimes_{R^a_{W,\bullet}}K$, termwise, and let $T_a$ be signed direct-sum total tensor. For fixed coefficients, $c_a:F_aT_a\cong T_a(F_a,F_a)$ is the normalized comparison [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence].

There are unique simultaneous natural chain isomorphisms $\kappa^{ab}:S_X^{ab}F_a\cong F_bS_Y^{ab}$ and $\sigma_W^{ab}:S_W^{ab}T_a\cong T_b(S_W^{ab},S_W^{ab})$ with the following local formulas in every sequence level and homogeneous bidegree (inverse-image notation on sections is suppressed):
$$\kappa^{ab}:b\otimes(a\otimes x)\longmapsto b\,i_X^{ab}(a)\otimes(1\otimes x),\qquad
(\kappa^{ab})^{-1}:b\otimes(d\otimes x)\longmapsto b\,\phi^b(d)\otimes(1\otimes x),$$
$$\sigma_W^{ab}:b\otimes(x\otimes y)\longmapsto(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y),\qquad
(\sigma_W^{ab})^{-1}:(b\otimes x)\otimes(d\otimes y)\longmapsto bd\otimes(x\otimes y).$$
Here $a$ is an $R^a_X$ coefficient and $d$ in the inverse formula for $\kappa$ is a section of $u^{-1}R^b_Y$; all formulas denote generalized local tensor generators after sheafification. Together with $c_a$, these maps and their inverses are maps of strict systems, preserving both differential summands $dx\otimes y$ and $(-1)^p x\otimes dy$ for $x\in K^p$. They satisfy
$$c_b\,F_b(\sigma_Y^{ab})\,\kappa^{ab}_{T_a(K,H)}
=T_b(\kappa_K^{ab},\kappa_H^{ab})\,\sigma_X^{ab}\,S_X^{ab}(c_a).$$
Both composites send $b\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. This is equality of chain maps and hence of their inverse chain maps, retaining every sequence transition.

Let $U_W^a:S_W^{aa}\cong1$ be $a\otimes x\mapsto ax$ and $A_W:S_W^{12}S_W^{01}\cong S_W^{02}$ be $d\otimes(b\otimes x)\mapsto d\,i_W^{12}(b)\otimes x$. Under $U$, $\kappa^{aa}$ and $\sigma^{aa}$ are identities. Under $A$, the composite $S_X^{12}S_X^{01}F_0\to S_X^{12}F_1S_Y^{01}\to F_2S_Y^{12}S_Y^{01}$ equals $\kappa^{02}$, and the composite $S_W^{12}S_W^{01}T_0\to S_W^{12}T_1(S_W^{01},S_W^{01})\to T_2(S_W^{12}S_W^{01},S_W^{12}S_W^{01})$ equals $\sigma_W^{02}$. In the latter equality both routes on $d\otimes(b\otimes(x\otimes y))$ have value $(d\,i_W^{12}(b)\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. The unit, composition, and square equations hold in strict systems, in both directions. No boundedness, flatness, normalization, or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed.
